extraction.narrative:
# DISCHARGE SUMMARY

**PATIENT INFORMATION**
Name: John Smith
Age: 65 years
Medical Record Number: Not documented
Admission Date: January 15, 2024
Surgery Date: January 16, 2024
Discharge Date: January 19, 2024
Length of Stay: 4 days

**DIAGNOSES**
Primary Diagnosis: Right frontal lesion

**HOSPITAL COURSE**

Mr. Smith is a 65-year-old patient who presented to the hospital on January 15, 2024, with a chief complaint of headaches. On admission, neurological examination revealed a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15 with the patient alert and oriented. Examination was notable for mild right-sided weakness with strength documented at 4+/5.

The patient underwent right frontal craniotomy on January 16, 2024, for resection of the right frontal lesion. The procedure was performed without documented intraoperative complications.

Post-operatively, the patient progressed well over the subsequent three days. By the time of discharge on post-operative day 3, the patient demonstrated neurological improvement with resolution of the previously noted weakness. Discharge neurological examination revealed the patient to be alert and oriented to person, place, and time with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15. Motor examination showed improvement in right upper extremity strength to 5-/5, and the patient was moving all extremities well.

The hospital course was otherwise uncomplicated with no documented post-operative complications.

**DISCHARGE STATUS**

Neurological Status: Glasgow Coma Scale 15, alert and oriented x3
Motor Examination: Moving all extremities well; right arm strength 5-/5
Functional Status: Karnofsky Performance Status 80, modified Rankin Scale 1, ECOG Performance Status 1

**DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS**
1. Levetiracetam (Keppra) 1000 mg by mouth twice daily
2. Dexamethasone 4 mg by mouth every 6 hours

**FOLLOW-UP**
Follow-up arrangements were not documented in the available clinical data.

**ACTIVITY AND RESTRICTIONS**
Activity restrictions were not documented in the available clinical data.
